newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FARMA TO LAUNCH DRUG STORES IN MOSCOW.
newsitem.headline: FARMA TO LAUNCH DRUG STORES IN MOSCOW.

text.p: Estonia's Tallinna Farmaatsiatehas said on Tuesday it will launch a drug store chain in Moscow with a Russian investment company.
"The project cost is about $1.5 million and payback time is two years according to the business plan," it added in a statement.
Farmaatsiatehas added the project will probably be financed by an Estonian commercial bank.
The company said it will have ten drug stores districts of Moscow with about five million inhabitants.

The drug store chain will belong to a joint-stock company, which will be owned at least 50 percent by Farmaatsiatehas. The rest will be owned by a Russian investment company and probably by a Scandinavian drug store chain.
